correctness.rationale: For every vertex survivor subset the maximum induced-component order is computed exactly. A complete AHU canonical tree enumeration through eight vertices, justified by leaf removal/extension, yields class counts (1,1,1,2,3,6,11,23) and same-degree comparison counts (0,0,0,0,0,1,5,23); all six comparisons through order seven are coordinatewise comparable. The two three-arm order-eight trees have exact survivor-total vectors (0,8,35,98,167,177,119,46,8) and (0,8,35,98,167,178,118,46,8), confirmed by independent union-find for all 512 subsets each. Their sole nonzero difference at k=5,6 is (-1,+1), yielding the exact unrestricted expectation difference p^5(1-p)^2(2p-1). Uniqueness among order-eight same-degree incomparable pairs follows from comparing every one of 23 pairs. The finite scope and use of integer-exhaustive data, not sampled experiments, are explicit.

originality.rationale: Mathematical-record queries and inspected ecological/graph-theoretic primary literature were compared by implication. The source ecological network-measure taxonomy does not state an exact degree-matched reversal; the fixed-degree tree extremality theorem treats different invariants and does not entail conditional largest surviving-component ordering, while site percolation on random recursive trees is an asymptotic random-tree analysis. The nearest prior finite-network results concerned number of components, protected-site selection or one-guild survival, not two equal-degree tree networks under homogeneous site percolation. No identified source implies the complete sharp eight-vertex reversal and one-pair classification. The originality assessment remains provisional to independent bibliographic audit, with a documented risk of overlooked graph-polynomial representations.

value.rationale: The largest surviving habitat component measures the largest contiguous habitat block after patch loss. Restricting tree designs to one degree multiset controls local link counts and reveals the smallest nontrivial structural failure of a survival-parameter-independent design ranking. The exact sharp eight-vertex cutoff, uniqueness among degree-matched incomparabilities of that size, and algebraic half-survival crossing are a motivated network-vulnerability result that is not merely a renamed tree count or an arbitrary fixed-probability calculation; no extension to general graphs or heterogeneously weighted patches is implied.
